purpose: D9 demand-built cache vs D8 eager cache, with fresh D7/D9 native controls; exploratory diagnostic, not upstream NI
pairing: before=D8/after=D9 except native_reference before=D7; cold_perturbation both D9, before=phase timer off/after=on. One common executable per phase, old public APIs only.
sampling: 8 independent process pairs per bucket, rotating buckets and alternating pair order, no profiler or concurrent build/tests. Every rate window >=200ms. All pairs retained.
warm: Same 18 payload/binding-warm facade fixtures as D8, exact generic requests/page 0 on D8 and D9. Per-operation capture/release included.
cold: N64 pages rewritten/published to fresh generations each cycle, K0 (no new read), K1 or K16 first read then session release. CPU/tiles3, BPP4/16. Initial configure/fill and final close separate, lifecycle CPU/wall also recorded. Old-version GC occurs during subsequent commits. Two cold stats checks/Qt correctness assertions per cycle are included on both sides.
profile: cold_profile compares D8/D9 with phase clocks enabled; separate cold_perturbation compares plain/profile D9 in paired runs. Inclusive prepare+publish and first-read-scope sums are diagnostic, not exact binding/lock self, not additive to lifecycle elapsed time or single-event latency. K1 intervals may approach timer overhead; retain limitation.
stopping: Stop on nonzero test exit, wrong loader, source/runtime change, counter mismatch, duplicate/missing row, or short rate window. Keep partial output. Do not alter frozen protocol after inspecting results.
limitations: No pre-frozen NI margin, upstream current comparison, single-operation tails, high-H/concurrent performance, or full background drain. Count/byte zero does not prove UMA performance. Allocation records and shared gates unchanged; only native read-cache population policy is treated. Later structural changes require a new slice.
